project_dependencies.use: Frozen 5.2.37–38 cases and different spellings of the elephant series.
PG782 owns the palm-height reference and the separate chest adjective.
PG271 explicitly registers bare optative cinvīta and the bare present cinute.
The monthly and Aṅgiras extensions have older ownership.
Stable identities for feminine selection, stem preservation and vowel shortening.
Full PG14 operator, histories and pairing.

source_observations.observation: The nominative supplies a standard and the genitive the measured bearer. Dvayasac and daghnac select height. Mātrac also takes other standards including volume. Exact and doubtful amount, conventionally named units and their luk conditions have separate statements.

source_observations.locator: Mahābhāṣya 5.2.37, vārttika and discussion following the heading
source_observations.observation: The discussion explicitly asks whether the standard qualifies the suffix meaning or the base. It makes the measure qualify the input and spells out the possessor of the measure.
Aṇ adds a fourth choice on human and elephant standards. Preserve the n of hastin in hāstina under 6.4.164. Frozen examples attest dvihastinī and trihastinī.
A moat measured by two people has a long ā or a long ī in the feminine. Purchase and mere aggregation have different conditioning.
Feminine ṅīp after an n-final stem. This is the source Nyāsa invokes for the elephant noun.
The altar is the entity built. Stage one is knee height, stage two navel height and stage three neck height. A distinct series in the preceding section counts the bricks.
Each height is segmented. The last standard has grīva with short final a. Cinvīta and cinvānaḥ are separate. The ascent predicate is marked as a sequence containing abhi and ārohati.
Names the height suffix by quoting 5.2.37. Explains the short vowel in grīva under 6.3.63. In the preceding clause he explains the thousand bricks and explicitly supplies masculine agnim.
A knee-deep altar bed is dug. The adjective agrees with uttaravedīm, feminine accusative. In 1.25.3 the bare present cinute is witnessed.

source_observations.locator: Commentaries on Āpastamba Śulbasūtra, discussion of height and brick number
source_observations.observation: The third height is glossed with āsya, the face or mouth. Height and brick count are separately described.

source_observations.locator: Vārāha Śrautasūtra, Cayana adhyāya 2 khaṇḍa 2, clauses 21–22, printed p. 78
source_observations.observation: The third landmark is printed चबुक in the height series. The brick numbers occur in the following clause.
The human bearer is described with a fully grown palm as the height standard. Its earlier source mention and the broad chest receive zero repeat credit.
The thumb supplies the standard in aṅguṣṭhamātraḥ. Puruṣaḥ is the measured subject in agreement.
Class-one active entry 01.0195. With abhi and ā the Taittirīya clause expresses ascending.
Ordinary present active jayati with abhi as a separate word in this Vedic clause.
